A free public guide for painters, students and visitors, and for the shops, schools and galleries that keep Cape Ann's art community going. It grew from a research brief on American painters' views of Gloucester, Massachusetts: 131 works in public collections, 42 shown in public-domain images, and nine sites where a painting can be tied to a standing point on the ground.

Sun position uses the NOAA solar position equations for the painter's standing point, in Gloucester local time (Eastern, with daylight saving applied automatically). Sunrise and sunset are when the sun's upper edge meets the horizon, allowing for refraction. Results agree with the brief's 2027 tables to within a minute. Terrain, buildings and trees are not modeled, so a hill or a seawall can hide a low sun earlier than shown.

Coastline from MassGIS (Census 2020 town outlines); the dashed brown line is the MassGIS historic high-water line, showing the shore before filling. Place points from OpenStreetMap. Distances and bearings are great-circle figures from true north.

Only public-domain images are reproduced, each credited to its source in the viewer. Works still under copyright, or whose museum does not release the image, are listed with a link to the museum's own page. Every work links to its collection record; numbered notes open the full citation.

Drag or pinch to move the map; scroll or use + and − to zoom. Choose a site to see the view line, then move the time slider or change the date to watch the sun move. Open any painting full screen and pinch or scroll to look closely. Every site and painting has its own link, so you can share exactly what you are looking at.

Allow location to see where you are on the chart, how far you are from each vantage point, and to stamp your passport on the spot. Allow the camera to line a painting up with the real view and make a then-and-now postcard. Nothing leaves your phone: location, photos and passport stamps stay in your browser.

After your first visit the chart, sun planner, passport and the paintings for the nine sites are kept on your device, so the guide opens with no connection. Before you head for the shore, save the rest of the paintings too. On a phone, choose ⟦0⟧Add to Home Screen⟦1⟧ from the browser's share or menu button to keep the guide as an app.

Which great American painters worked in Gloucester and on Cape Ann, Massachusetts, and where their pictures hang today

From Fitz Henry Lane’s harbor of the 1840s to Rothko’s wharfs and Nell Blaine’s Rocky Neck, Gloucester and Cape Ann drew painters for more than a hundred years. This brief catalogues their pictures, says where each one hangs, and maps nine places where you can stand where they stood.
